n: Because the Son is so great, we must pay closer attention to what we have heard, so we don’t drift away like a boat slipping past its harbor.
If the message delivered through angels — the law of Moses — was binding, and every violation was justly punished,

f.g: Jewish tradition held that angels helped deliver the law at Sinai.

n: how can we escape if we ignore such a great salvation? The Lord Himself first announced it, and those who heard Him confirmed it to us.

f.g: The eyewitnesses — suggesting the author was a second-generation believer.

n: God also testified to it with signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost distributed as He chose.
God did not give the angels rule over the world to come, which is the subject here.

f.g: The coming age of Christ’s reign.

n: Someone has testified in the Psalms: “What is man that you remember him, or the son of man that you care for him?”
“You made him a little lower than the angels for a while, crowned him with glory and honor, and put him over your works.”

f.w: a little lower than the angels

n: God put everything under humanity’s feet. Yet we don’t see everything under man’s control now — the promise is not yet fulfilled in us.
But we do see Jesus, made lower than the angels for a while so He could suffer death, now crowned with glory and honor. By God’s grace He tasted death for everyone. He fulfills Psalm 8 for us.
It was fitting for God, who created and sustains all things, to make the leader of our salvation complete through suffering, as He brings many children to glory.

f.g: Fully qualified, complete — not that He was ever sinful.

n: Jesus, who makes people holy, and those being made holy share one Father. So He is not ashamed to call them brothers and sisters.

f.w: not ashamed to call them brethren

n: As the Psalm says, “I will declare your name to my brothers; in the congregation I will sing your praise.” Psalm 22 begins with the cry Jesus uttered on the cross.

f.w: I will declare thy name unto my brethren

n: And Isaiah: “I will put my trust in Him,” and “Here am I, and the children God has given me.” Christ stands with His people as one family.

f.w: I will put my trust in him

n: Since God’s children have flesh and blood, Jesus took on the same, so that by His death He could break the power of the devil, who held the power of death.
And set free those who all their lives were enslaved by the fear of death.
He came not to help angels, but to help Abraham’s descendants — human beings.

f.g: Took hold of, came to help.

n: So He had to become like His brothers and sisters in every way, to be a merciful and faithful High Priest who makes atonement for the people’s sins. This introduces the book’s main theme: Christ as High Priest.
Because He Himself suffered when tempted, He can help those who are tempted. He knows from experience.
